reason: E1 directly supports M–N bond formation, sintering resistance, and durability enhancement in a multi-element alloy, but only for electrocatalytic ORR, not automotive exhaust. E2 and E3 provide no evidence for nitrogen doping or M–N bonds; they address configurational disorder in spinel oxides and Pd single-atom stability, respectively, and are misapplied to support the key premises.
premises: Nitrogen doping forms stable M–N bonds on multi-element alloy surfaces
M–N bonds anchor metal atoms and prevent sintering
M–N bonds enhance corrosion resistance and durability
Nitrogen doping boosts catalytic activity and durability via lattice distortion
These effects are transferable from electrocatalytic ORR to automotive exhaust catalysis
